title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All of Light & Wonder's Directors, employees, consultants and independent contractors engaged by Light & Wonder. Section 3 restrictions (inside information, front page test, no speculative dealing/short selling, publicly traded options, hedging and monetisation, standing orders, margin accounts and pledging) apply to this whole tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, Senior Executives (other key management personnel including the CEO and any direct reports to the CEO), Section 16 Officers and Nominated Employees. Only this tier is subject to the section 4 blackout periods and prior approval requirement.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; a component of Restricted Persons, separately subject to prompt post-trade notification to the Chief Legal Officer and to US Section 16 and Rule 144 obligations.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Other key management personnel of Light & Wonder, including the CEO and any other direct reports to the CEO; a component of Restricted Persons with no separate rules.

tiers.name: Section 16 Officers
tiers.description: Officers subject to Section 16 of the US Securities Exchange Act of 1934; a component of Restricted Persons, separately subject to post-trade notification, Form 4 filing, short-swing profit disgorgement and the statutory short sale ban.

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Other persons who regularly possess, or by virtue of their position are likely to have access to, Inside Information and who have been advised by the Chief Legal Officer that they are subject to special restrictions; a component of Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Family members residing with the Employee and others living in the household; family members outside the household whose covered transactions are directed by, subject to the influence or control of, or financially dependent on the Employee; any other person who may reasonably be expected to influence or be influenced by the Employee in relation to Company securities; and trusts or other entities controlled by the Employee or a household member. The same restrictions apply to them as to the Employee.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on the last day of the applicable fiscal quarter
windows.end_anchor: after the close of one full trading day on the ASX as well as one full trading day on a US national securities exchange following the public release of the Company's financial results for that quarter

windows.start_anchor: the day after release of the Company's full-year, half-year or first and third quarter results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chief Legal Officer may specify any other blackout period from time to time (for example while material non-public information is being assembled for release, or during a material event known only to a few directors or executives). Confidential: the existence of an event-specific blackout will not be announced other than to those aware of the triggering event and to Restricted Persons, and must not be disclosed to anyone else.

rules.detail: Absolute ban for every Employee and Connected Person on transactions in exchange-traded or other organised-market puts, calls or derivative securities over Company securities. No vesting distinction, no approval route and no exemption; section 5 excluded dealings disapply only sections 4.1 and 4.3.
rules.evidence: Employees may not engage in transactions in publicly traded options in the Company's securities, such as puts, calls or derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market.

rules.detail: A bilateral OTC put or call with a bank is not a 'publicly traded option' and so falls outside 3.4, but any OTC derivative that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities, or is designed to offset a decrease in their market price, is prohibited hedging under 3.5. The definition of securities expressly includes put and call options whether or not issued by the Company, so an OTC option is itself a Company security and dealing in it by a Restricted Person would also require approval and fall in blackouts were it not already banned.
rules.evidence: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on arrangements that limit the economic risk of holding Company securities. The policy draws no distinction between unvested, vested-but-locked and freely held securities, applies to Connected Persons, and provides no clearance or hardship route out of section 3.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities. You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation transactions are named alongside hedging and banned outright, so a prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar cash-out structure is prohibited for all Employees irrespective of vesting or tier.
rules.evidence: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Speculative dealing is banned and short selling is named as an instance of it; the policy defines short selling as borrowing and selling securities to buy them back lower.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Directors and Section 16 Officers are additionally responsible for the statutory US restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities under Section 16 of the Exchange Act.
rules.evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits" and restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities)

rules.detail: Lending out Company securities is never mentioned; borrowing securities appears only in the descriptive definition of short selling. The dealing definition (purchases, sales, gifts, donations, acquisitions, disposals and option exercises) does not sweep in a securities loan, although a lending arrangement that transferred title would be a disposal.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Company securities is speculative dealing, is a derivative security if written on an organised market, and if short is both a hedge of a decrease in price and economically a short sale, so it is caught by three separate bans.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Holding Company securities in a margin account is prohibited for all Employees and Connected Persons. The only carve-out is the cashless exercise of options, where shares underlying the option are sold to fund tax, the exercise price and broker commissions.
rules.evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.detail: Pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan is expressly banned. A charge, lien or security interest unconnected with a loan is not named, and granting security is not part of the dealing definition, so it is only caught if it amounts to a pledge for a loan.
rules.evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.detail: Any loan collateralised by Company securities is prohibited, not merely a margin loan. The ban sits in section 3 (all Employees), has no tier or vesting carve-out, and is not among the section 5 excluded dealings, which relieve only the blackout and approval requirements in sections 4.1 and 4.3.
rules.evidence: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.detail: No holding period or minimum interval is set. The restraint is qualitative: dealing on a speculative basis is banned, reinforced by the Front Page Test, and approval will not be granted where a dealing would fail that test.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling.

rules.detail: Directors and Section 16 Officers must comply with the US short-swing profit rule, under which profits on a purchase and sale (in either order) matched within six months are disgorgeable. This is imported by reference rather than being stated as a policy holding period.
rules.evidence: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of "short-swing profits" ...) and Rule 144 of the Securities Act of 1933 in connection with their transactions in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Restricted Persons inherit every section 3 prohibition and add blackout periods and prior approval. Even if a derivative escaped sections 3.4 and 3.5, it would be a dealing in securities (the definition of securities includes put and call options whether or not issued by the Company) requiring Chief Legal Officer approval and barred in the quarterly and event-specific blackouts.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.1, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: Chief Legal Officer (or the CEO where the request is made by the Chief Legal Officer); the Chief Legal Officer may delegate and must do so if uncontactable for an extended period
clearance.evidence: Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.

clearance.post_trade_to: Chief Legal Officer (and Form 4 with the SEC)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered; Form 4 within two business days of most transactions
clearance.evidence: Following any trade, Directors and Section 16 Officers must promptly notify the Chief Legal Officer, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered.

clearance.post_trade_to: Chief Legal Officer (and Form 4 with the SEC; Form 144 before certain open market sales)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered; Form 4 within two business days of most transactions
clearance.evidence: This includes filing a Form 4 with the SEC within two business days of most transactions in Company securities (including gifts), and filing a Form 144 prior to certain open market sale of Company shares.

exceptions.approver: Chief Legal Officer (or CEO if the applicant is the Chief Legal Officer); waivers reported to the Board at the next scheduled board meeting
exceptions.evidence: If a Restricted Person needs to deal in securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances and is not in possession of any Inside Information, then, they may apply for approval to deal. Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company, including: purchases of Company securities under the employee share purchase plan resulting from an employee's periodic payroll contributions; the exercise of a share option for cash; and the issuance of shares upon vesting of an award of restricted share units (RSUs)

acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of Company securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of Company securities through a rights issue
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of merger consideration, a scheme of arrangement or tender offer/equal access buy-back.

Dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary).

exceptions.approver: pre-approved; the plan must not be entered into or amended during a blackout
exceptions.evidence: Trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chief Legal Officer approves the steps taken by the donor
exceptions.evidence: Bona fide gifts of the Company's securities where the donor has taken appropriate steps approved by the Chief Legal Officer to ensure that the recipient will not sell the Company's securities while the donor is aware or in possession of Inside Information.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Standing orders are banned outright: 'You may not place standing orders (e.g. open orders at set prices) involving Company securities. A broker-executed standing order while you hold Inside Information may result in unlawful trading.' Price-triggered execution is therefore unavailable except under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan entered outside a blackout.

exemption_authority: Chief Legal Officer (CEO where the Chief Legal Officer is the applicant) may approve a Restricted Person's dealing during a blackout in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or court order, on sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action; waivers are reported to the Board at its next scheduled meeting. There is no exemption authority at all for the section 3 prohibitions (speculative dealing, publicly traded options, hedging, monetisation, standing orders, margin accounts and pledging): section 5 excluded dealings disapply only sections 4.1 and 4.3.
jurisdiction_overlays: US federal securities law: Exchange Act Section 16 (short-swing profit disgorgement, short sale restrictions, Form 4 within two business days), Rule 144 and Form 144, Regulation FD, and 'material non-public information' read as equivalent to Inside Information

Australian law: Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) insider trading provisions and the ASX Listing Rules; the blackout end anchor requires a full trading day on both the ASX and a US national securities exchange

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to the following: ... [excluded dealings]. Exceptional circumstances relief in section 4.2 is likewise expressed as relief to 'deal in securities during a blackout period'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every relief mechanism in the policy operates only on the blackout and approval requirements, so the hedging, monetisation, publicly traded options and pledging bans that kill a funded collar cannot be waived by anyone, including the Board.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may not enter into hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put leg of a collar is the paradigm arrangement designed to offset a decrease in market price, and the word 'monetisation' independently captures the funded element, so the structure is prohibited on its face for all Employees and Connected Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may not hold the Company's securities in a margin account or pledge the Company's securities as collateral for a loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is separately and expressly prohibited, so even an unfunded collar could not be financed against the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees may not engage in transactions in publicly traded options in the Company's securities, such as puts, calls or derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Listed puts and calls are barred outright, and while a bilateral bank OTC option is not 'publicly traded', the substance over form statement means the Company will look through an OTC wrapper used to achieve the same result.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A structure engineered to sit outside the literal words (for example a bespoke OTC collar, a Connected Person entity, or a non-recourse loan documented as a sale) will still be assessed on its economic substance as hedging or monetisation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a dealing that is technically permitted must survive a reputational test, and a bank-funded collar over executive shares is precisely the kind of transaction that would fail it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may not place standing orders (e.g. open orders at set prices) involving Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Price-triggered or knock-in/knock-out features and automatic delivery mechanics would need to be recast as a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, which cannot be entered into or amended during a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must ensure that their Connected Persons only deal in securities when the Employee to whom they are connected would be permitted to do so under this Policy. The same restrictions that apply to Employees apply equally to their Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a controlled trust, household member or influenced family member does not escape any of the prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Section 16 Officers are also responsible for compliance with Section 16 of the Exchange Act (including provisions related to disgorgement of 'short-swing profits' and restrictions on short sales of the Company's securities).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For US-reporting insiders the put and call legs are themselves Section 16 derivative securities: entering, amending or settling them creates reportable transactions that can be matched against ordinary purchases within six months, generating disgorgement risk independent of the ASX policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved leg of a multi-step structure can be pulled without reasons before execution, and the five business day approval life means a cleared trade must be priced and closed quickly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A breach can extinguish the very shares that collateralise the bank's loan, so the bank's security is exposed to a disciplinary outcome rather than only market risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are aware of Inside Information when your employment or engagement ends, you must not trade until that information becomes public and one full trading day has elapsed, or it ceases to be material.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Departure does not immediately free an executive to enter or unwind a structure, though the section 3 bans are framed as applying to Employees and so would fall away on cessation.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy at any tier or vesting state. Section 3.5 expressly prohibits every Employee, Director, consultant and Connected Person from entering hedging or monetisation transactions or similar arrangements designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market price of the Company's securities, which captures the purchased put and the collar as a whole, and separately prohibits holding Company securities in a margin account or pledging them as collateral for a loan, which kills the secured loan leg. Section 3.4 independently bans transactions in publicly traded puts, calls and derivative securities on an exchange or any other organised market, and although a bilateral OTC option with a bank is not literally 'publicly traded', the Company's stated substance over form approach and the Front Page Test mean an OTC wrapper achieving the same economics would still be treated as a breach. None of these prohibitions can be waived: the exceptional circumstances relief in section 4.2 and the excluded dealings in section 5 disapply only the section 4.1 blackout and the section 4.3 approval requirement, so there is no exemption authority for section 3 and no hardship route. For US-reporting Directors and Section 16 Officers, the option legs would in any event be reportable derivative securities exposed to short-swing profit disgorgement and the statutory short sale restrictions.
